question: PATROLTRACK read whole - who is told, its values, province, countries and Goto - and what EXPRETURNED / EXPRETURNEDWE carry for their unit Goto.

addresses.name: CPatrolOrder::UpdateShadow
addresses.comment: **Which fleet a patrol shadows**, every hour after its move. The one it shadowed has its byte CUnit +0x95 cleared and the reference at +0x48 is emptied. Then the first unit in the patrol's province, in list order, that is another country's fleet, in range by the order's slot 8, not of the patrol's faction and with no friendly agreement (CDiplomacyStatus::HasFriendlyAgreement), and that ShouldStartNavalCombat(patrol, it) sights: the reference becomes it and its +0x95 is set; a new one for the player's patrol raises the message PATROLTRACK. **No war is asked for.** The reference is what the intelligence refresh reads to give the country level 9 of the province. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-navalmissions.md, section 4. The friendly agreement is CDiplomacyStatus::HasFriendlyAgreement (0x64A680, call at 0x19D08E) of the other fleet's country's record towards the patrol's; the faction test needs the other's faction real (slot 7) and equal (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 41). **PATROLTRACK, read whole 2026-11-14** (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-navalmissions.md, section 4): 'a new one' is the found fleet's persistent id set against the reference's id as the function was entered (copied to locals before the old shadow is let go), so the same fleet found again the next hour raises nothing, and a fleet found after an hour of shadowing nobody raises it again. Only where the game state's player id is the patrol's owner's (+0x128). Values: CCountry::BuildMessageVariables of the player's country; MONARCHTITLE = CCountry_GetRulerTitle of the patrol's owner; OUR_FLEET = the patrol's name (CUnit slot 7, GetName); OTHER = CountryNameOfTag of the shadowed fleet's owner (+0x124); OTHERS = the shadowed fleet's own name (slot 7) - which the text 'found $OTHERS$ fleet' reads as an adjective; PROV = the name of the shadowed fleet's province (+0x130, the province's GetName through its base at +8). CMessage(FindType('PATROLTRACK'), vars, the patrol's province (+0x130), '', 0, first = the patrol's owner (+0x124/+0x128), second = the shadowed fleet's owner, **the patrol's persistent id (+0x10/+0x14) in the reserved arguments 11 and 12**), posted with CMessageHandler::GotoProvinceForMessage - so it carries the patrol, but its Goto centres on the province. The answer is true once a fleet is taken up, false when none is.
addresses.revises: comment only: adds PATROLTRACK's test of a new one, its six values, its province, countries, unit id and Goto
addresses.evidence: Decompiled 2026-11-14 (VA 0x59CE10) and listed 0x59CE10-0x59D810: local_74/local_70 = order+0x4C/+0x50 at entry; the raise sits inside `if (local_70 != order+0x50 || local_74 != order+0x4C)` and `if (player.id == patrol+0x128)`; string pushes 'MONARCHTITLE', 'OUR_FLEET', 'OTHER', 'OTHERS', 'PROV', 'PATROLTRACK' (0x59D79D) in that order; at 0x59D7EF-0x59D808 `mov edx,[eax+0x10]; sub esp,0x78; ... sub esp,8; mov [ecx],edx; mov eax,[eax+0x14]; mov [ecx+4],eax` with eax = order+8, the patrol. Shown wrong by a second raise in the body, or by the compare reading the reference after it is cleared.

addresses.name: CUnit::ReturnFromExpedition
addresses.comment: **An expeditionary unit goes back to the country that lent it.** 0x5020E0 to the single `ret 4` at 0x502BB3. `this` the unit, `host` the country it served. In order: CUnit_LeaveParent(unit, 1); the unit unlinked from its lender's (expeditionary_owner +0x28C) list of units lent out (CCountry +0xBBC); expeditionary_owner set to `---`/0; an AI agent (+0x198) detached through its slot 64 (+0x100); 0x8A2E00; the unit unlinked from its owner's units (+0xBAC) and CCountry::AddUnit(lender, unit); 0x5D3840(unit, &lender, 1); CUnit::RebuildAvatar; CUnit::EnterProvince(its province); its intel_level (+0x1F8) recomputed for the player (9 where 0x5D37D0 says so, else the province's intel byte) and avatar_stale set when it changed. Then, **only where the local player is the host or the lender**, a message with ACTOR (the host's name), RECIPIENT (the lender's), MESSENGER and NAME (the unit's name, slot 7), at the unit's province: **EXPRETURNEDWE** to the host's player ('We returned an expeditionary force to $RECIPIENT$.'), else **EXPRETURNED** to the lender's ('$ACTOR$ returned an expeditionary force to us.'). Callers: AnnexCountry twice (0x4E8690, 0x4E86D3), SetGovernmentInExile (0x502DFB) and the country's daily pass (0x4DB418, with the unit in ECX - FINDINGS-distribute.md's '0x5020E0(country)' left out the unit). The name is ours. **The message read on the listing 2026-11-14** (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-expedition.md): the variables are CCountry::BuildMessageVariables of the player's country, then ACTOR = CountryNameOfCountry(host), RECIPIENT = CountryNameOfTag(lender), MESSENGER = MESSAGE_HEAD_CHAN, NAME = the unit's GetName; both raises are CMessage(type, vars, the unit's province (+0x130, read after the hand-over), '', 0, first = the host, second = the lender, **the unit's persistent id (+0x10/+0x14) in the reserved arguments 11 and 12**), posted with CMessageHandler::GotoUnitForMessage - which finds the unit by that id through the persistent table, whoever owns it by then (the lender).
addresses.revises: comment only: adds the message's variables in order, its province, its two countries and the unit id it carries for its Goto
addresses.evidence: Decompiled and listed 2026-11-14 (VA 0x5020E0-0x502BB3): string pushes 'ACTOR' (0x5022DB), 'RECIPIENT' (0x50246C), 'MESSAGE_HEAD_CHAN' (0x5025F0), 'MESSENGER' (0x50260F), 'NAME' (0x502806), 'EXPRETURNEDWE' (0x5029B7); at 0x5029D8-0x5029F0 `mov ecx,[edi+0x10]; ... sub esp,8; mov [eax],ecx; mov edx,[edi+0x14]; mov [eax+4],edx` and `mov edi,[edi+0x130]` with edi = this; the host's +0xCA4/+0xCA8 pushed as arguments 7 and 8. Confidence left as recorded (inferred) for the rest of the body, which this reading did not revisit. Shown wrong by a third raise, or the id being someone else's.

addresses.name: CMessage::CMessage
addresses.no_signature: Twelve arguments of which several are only passed on, and two are a reserved eight bytes rather than pushes. Writing it out would type four things as ints that have not been identified; the order is in the comment, which is what a caller needs.
addresses.comment:
**Builds a message**, into the 0x80 buffer its first argument points at. Twelve arguments, `ret 0x30`, in the order CCountry::ShatterUnit pushes them:

    1  the buffer to build into
    2  the type, from CMessageHandler::FindType   -> +0x20
    3  the variable list, which it walks and releases
    4  the province                                -> +0x44
    5  a head string, which CCountry::ShatterUnit passes **empty**
    6  zero                                        -> +0x70
    7,8   the first country's tag and id           -> +0x34, +0x38
    9,10  the second country's tag and id          -> +0x3C, +0x40
    11,12 a unit's persistent id, type and id      -> +0x68, +0x6C

Arguments 11 and 12 are not pushed: they are eight bytes the caller reserves below the ten that are (`sub esp,8`) and fills by `mov` - zero in CCountry::ShatterUnit's, **the unit's +0x10/+0x14** in CUnit::ReturnFromExpedition's and CPatrolOrder::UpdateShadow's. CMessageHandler::GotoUnitForMessage finds the unit by them. The body is a plain field setter. Read again 2026-11-14 (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-messages.md).
addresses.revises: comment only: arguments 11 and 12 are a unit's persistent id filled into the reserved bytes by the caller, not always zero; arguments 7-10 named as the two countries
addresses.evidence: Listed 2026-11-14: CPatrolOrder::UpdateShadow at 0x59D7FE-0x59D808 and CUnit::ReturnFromExpedition at 0x5029E0-0x5029F0 both `sub esp,8` and store the unit's +0x10 and +0x14 into [esp] and [esp+4] before the ten pushes; GotoUnitForMessage (0x6996F0) reads +0x68/+0x6C into FindPersistentById. Shown wrong by the constructor storing arguments 11 and 12 anywhere but +0x68/+0x6C.

struct_fields.name: unit_type
struct_fields.comment: The persistent id's type half of the unit a message is about - constructor argument 11, filled by the caller into reserved stack bytes; 0 where it is about no unit. CMessageHandler::GotoUnitForMessage looks the unit up by this and +0x6C. Set by CUnit::ReturnFromExpedition (EXPRETURNED, EXPRETURNEDWE), CPatrolOrder::UpdateShadow (PATROLTRACK, whose Goto is the province's) and the arrival of a unit. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-messages.md.
struct_fields.evidence: GotoUnitForMessage (VA 0x6996F0) reads message+0x68 as the type and +0x6C as the id for FindPersistentById, high or low table by type < 0x1269 as every persistent lookup; the two raisers above store a unit's +0x10/+0x14 there. Shown wrong by another reader treating +0x68 otherwise.

struct_fields.name: unit_id
struct_fields.comment: The persistent id's id half of the unit a message is about - constructor argument 12; 0 with +0x68 where it is about no unit (GotoUnitForMessage then does nothing). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-messages.md.
struct_fields.evidence: As +0x68: GotoUnitForMessage tests `+0x6C == 0 && +0x68 == 0` for 'no unit' and passes both to FindPersistentById. Shown wrong by another reader.
